title: Croatian Government Scholarship for Croatian Diaspora and Croatian National Minorities
summary: This state scholarship supports members of the Croatian diaspora and Croatian national minorities abroad pursuing doctoral studies in Croatia. It provides monthly stipends, tuition coverage, and accommodation support. Administered by the Central State Office for Croats Abroad and the Ministry of Science and Education.

title: University of Zagreb Doctoral Scholarships (Doktorske stipendije)
summary: The University of Zagreb, Croatia's largest university, offers doctoral scholarships to enrolled PhD candidates across its faculties, including social sciences, law, and medicine relevant to humanitarian and global health research. Funding typically covers a monthly stipend and partial research costs. Applications are handled by individual faculties and doctoral schools.

title: Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts (HAZU) Research Assistant / Doctoral Positions
summary: HAZU and its associated research units occasionally offer doctoral research assistant positions funded through national research programmes. These positions support PhD candidates in social sciences, humanities, and biomedical research relevant to humanitarian and health fields. Positions are advertised periodically on the HAZU website and through partner institutions.

title: PhD Scholarship in International Studies
summary: The Graduate Institute's Doctoral School offers competitive PhD scholarships covering tuition and living stipends for candidates pursuing research in international studies, including humanitarian studies, forced migration, and global health. Scholarships are awarded based on academic merit and research potential.

key_figures.name: Vincent Chetail
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international refugee law, forced migration, and the legal protection of displaced persons. He directs the Global Migration Centre and works on the intersection of humanitarian law and migration governance.

key_figures.name: Davide Rodogno
key_figures.title: Professor of International History
key_figures.research_focus: Research examines the history of humanitarianism, humanitarian intervention, and international organizations. He studies forced migration and relief operations from the nineteenth century to the present.

key_figures.name: Jérôme Elie
key_figures.title: Senior Researcher and Lecturer
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on humanitarian action, forced migration, and the history and politics of refugee protection. He works on humanitarian studies and the evolution of refugee regimes.

title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship
summary: The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship is available to international PhD candidates, including those hosted at the Graduate Institute Geneva, covering monthly stipends, tuition, and insurance. It supports research in fields such as global health, humanitarian studies, and international humanitarian law.

key_figures.name: Sara E. Davies
key_figures.title: Professor of International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health governance, health security, and the politics of international responses to infectious disease outbreaks. Examines how states and international organizations manage public health emergencies.

key_figures.name: Andrew Clapham
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the regulation of armed conflict, including the law of occupation and accountability for violations. Has written extensively on the intersection of human rights and humanitarian law.

key_figures.name: Davide Rodogno
key_figures.title: Professor of International History
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the history of humanitarianism, humanitarian intervention, and international organizations. Examines the evolution of humanitarian action and relief practices from the nineteenth century to the present.

title: Doc.CH Scholarship
summary: Doc.CH is an SNSF funding scheme for doctoral candidates in the humanities and social sciences, including those at the Graduate Institute Geneva. It provides full salary support for research in areas such as humanitarian studies, international humanitarian law, and forced migration.

key_figures.name: Vincent Chetail
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, refugee law, and forced migration, with a focus on the legal protection of refugees and internally displaced persons.

key_figures.name: Davide Rodogno
key_figures.title: Professor of International History
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the history of humanitarianism, humanitarian intervention, and international humanitarian organizations, with attention to forced migration and relief practices.

key_figures.name: Jérôme Elie
key_figures.title: Senior Researcher and Lecturer
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on humanitarian action, forced migration, and the history and politics of refugee protection and humanitarian organizations.

title: Qatar Foundation Graduate Studies Scholarship (QF GSS)
summary: Qatar Foundation's Graduate Studies Scholarship provides full funding for outstanding students pursuing master's and doctoral degrees at QF partner universities in Education City, including Hamad Bin Khalifa University. It covers tuition, stipend, accommodation, and travel, and supports research aligned with QF's priority areas such as health, sustainability, and social sciences.

title: Hamad Bin Khalifa University PhD Scholarship
summary: Hamad Bin Khalifa University, a member of Qatar Foundation, offers fully-funded PhD scholarships across its doctoral programs, including in law, public policy, and health-related fields. The scholarship typically covers tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation, and research support for the duration of the doctoral program.

title: Qatar National Research Fund (QNRF) Graduate Research Sponsorship
summary: QNRF, a member of Qatar Foundation, funds research programs that support graduate students and doctoral researchers at QF institutions and partner universities in Qatar. Its grants support research in health, social sciences, and related priority areas, providing stipends and research funding for doctoral candidates.

title: Qatar University Graduate Scholarship (for QF-affiliated programs)
summary: Qatar University offers graduate scholarships, including doctoral funding, that are available to students in Qatar's higher education ecosystem, including those affiliated with Qatar Foundation institutions. These scholarships cover tuition and provide stipends for eligible PhD candidates in fields such as law, public health, and social sciences.

title: Fogarty Global Health Fellowship (FGHF)
summary: The Fogarty Global Health Fellowship supports predoctoral and postdoctoral trainees conducting mentored clinical research in low- and middle-income countries, including settings affected by conflict and humanitarian crises. Fellows receive stipend, travel, and research support for a year-long placement at an overseas site.

title: Fogarty HIV Research Training Program (FIC HIVRT)
summary: This Fogarty program funds institutional research training grants that support doctoral and postdoctoral trainees in HIV-related research at LMIC institutions, often in humanitarian and displacement-affected settings. Trainees receive tuition, stipend, and research costs through their host institution.

title: Fogarty Emerging Global Leader Award (K43)
summary: The K43 award provides mentored research funding for early-career scientists from LMICs working on global health topics, including disaster response and conflict-affected populations. It supports salary, research costs, and career development for up to five years.

title: Fogarty International Research Training Grants (D43)
summary: D43 training grants support doctoral and postdoctoral research training in global health at LMIC institutions, with tracks relevant to humanitarian crises and displacement. Trainees receive stipends, tuition, and research support through the grant.

title: Fogarty Global Health Equity Scholars Program (GHES)
summary: The GHES program funds predoctoral and postdoctoral fellows to conduct global health research at LMIC sites, including projects on disaster response and health in conflict. Fellows receive stipend, travel, and research support for a 12-month fellowship.

title: Aga Khan University PhD Fellowship in Health Sciences
summary: Aga Khan University offers fully-funded PhD fellowships in health sciences through its postgraduate medical education and research programmes, covering tuition, stipend, and research costs. Fellows conduct research in areas including public health, epidemiology, and health systems relevant to humanitarian and conflict-affected settings.

key_figures.name: Zulfiqar A. Bhutta
key_figures.title: Distinguished University Professor and Founding Director, Institute for Global Health and Development, Aga Khan University
key_figures.research_focus: Global maternal, newborn, and child health; nutrition; and health systems in low- and middle-income countries and conflict-affected settings. He leads large-scale global health research and policy initiatives, including work on evidence-based interventions for vulnerable populations.

key_figures.name: Sana Gul
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor, Department of Community Health Sciences, Aga Khan University
key_figures.research_focus: Public health and global health research with a focus on infectious disease epidemiology, maternal and child health, and health systems strengthening in Pakistan and other low-resource settings.

key_figures.name: Asad Mian
key_figures.title: Professor, Department of Emergency Medicine, Aga Khan University
key_figures.research_focus: Global health, emergency care, and health systems research, including innovation and capacity-building in low-resource and conflict-affected settings. His work addresses emergency and trauma care delivery in humanitarian contexts.

title: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme
summary: The Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme provides grants and loans to outstanding students from developing countries pursuing postgraduate studies, including PhDs, in fields such as health, development, and humanitarian studies. Awards are need-based and cover tuition and living expenses, typically on a partial basis with a loan component.

title: Aga Khan University Institute for Human Development PhD Studentship
summary: The Institute for Human Development at Aga Khan University supports doctoral research on human development, early childhood, and related social determinants of health, with relevance to displacement and vulnerable populations. Studentships typically include stipend and research support for full-time PhD candidates.

title: Aga Khan University PhD in Public Health (Fully-Funded Studentship)
summary: Aga Khan University's East Africa campus offers PhD training in public health and related disciplines with funded studentships covering fees, stipend, and research. Research themes include health systems, emergency and disaster response, and population health in low-resource settings.

title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) – Graduate Degree Program
summary: The Global Korea Scholarship (formerly Korean Government Scholarship Program, KGSP) is a fully-funded scholarship by the Korean government for international students pursuing master's and doctoral degrees at Korean universities. It covers tuition, living stipend, airfare, Korean language training, and settlement allowance. Applicants may pursue doctoral research in fields such as global health, international development, and public policy at participating Korean universities.

title: Korea Foundation for Advanced Studies (KFAS) Doctoral Fellowship
summary: The Korea Foundation for Advanced Studies offers doctoral fellowships to outstanding students, primarily Korean nationals, for advanced study in Korea and abroad. The fellowship supports research in social sciences, humanities, and related fields. It provides stipends and research support for doctoral candidates.

title: Korea Foundation Fellowship for Korean Studies
summary: The Korea Foundation offers fellowships for Korean studies research, including doctoral-level support for international scholars. Fellowships support research stays in Korea and can cover living expenses and research costs. Fields include social sciences and humanities relevant to Korean and international studies.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) – University Program
summary: The Chinese Government Scholarship University Program is administered by the China Scholarship Council (CSC) and funds full-time doctoral study at designated Chinese universities. It typically covers tuition, accommodation, stipend, and medical insurance, and can support PhD research in global health, public health, development, and related social science fields depending on the host university and supervisor.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) – Bilateral Program
summary: The CSC Bilateral Program is a full scholarship for international students pursuing doctoral degrees in China, based on educational cooperation agreements between China and other countries. Applicants apply through their home-country dispatching authorities, and eligible PhD topics can include global health, public health, disaster management, and international development studies.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) – Silk Road Program
summary: The CSC Silk Road Program supports doctoral students from Belt and Road countries to study at Chinese universities, with funding for tuition, living costs, and insurance. It can support PhD research in health, development, and related policy fields where the host university offers relevant doctoral supervision.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) – High-Level University Graduate Program
summary: This CSC program funds doctoral study at selected Chinese universities under the High-Level University Graduate Program. It provides full tuition, stipend, accommodation, and insurance, and may support PhD research in global health, public health, migration, and development-related fields depending on the host institution.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) – Chinese University Program
summary: The CSC Chinese University Program allows designated Chinese universities to recruit international PhD students with full CSC funding, including tuition, living allowance, and insurance. Relevant doctoral research may be possible in global health, public health, disaster management, and related law or policy areas where the university provides supervision.

title: Taiwan ICDF Higher Education Scholarship Program (PhD)
summary: The Taiwan ICDF Higher Education Scholarship Program funds outstanding international students from partner countries to pursue PhD degrees at selected Taiwanese universities. It covers tuition, airfare, housing, and a monthly stipend, with priority fields including public health, medicine, and disaster prevention. Applicants must apply through their country's government or a designated Taiwan ICDF partner institution.

title: Taiwan ICDF Scholarship for Master's and Doctoral Studies in Public Health
summary: This Taiwan ICDF scholarship stream supports doctoral and master's study in public health and related health sciences at partner universities in Taiwan. It is aimed at strengthening health systems in developing countries and covers tuition, living expenses, and travel. Candidates are typically nominated by their home governments.

title: Taiwan ICDF Scholarship in Disaster Risk Reduction and Management
summary: The Taiwan ICDF offers fully-funded doctoral and master's scholarships in disaster risk reduction and management fields at selected Taiwanese universities. The program targets professionals from developing countries to build capacity in disaster preparedness and response. Funding includes tuition, stipend, insurance, and return airfare.

title: ICCR Scholarship Scheme for Doctoral Studies (PhD) in India
summary: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) administers scholarship schemes for international students, including doctoral-level study at Indian universities under its General Scholarship Scheme and various bilateral cultural exchange programmes. Awards typically cover tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation allowance, and other costs for the full duration of the PhD. Applicants apply through Indian diplomatic missions in their home country.

title: ICCR General Scholarship Scheme (Doctoral Level)
summary: Under the General Scholarship Scheme, ICCR offers fully-funded slots to international students, including at PhD level, at participating Indian universities across disciplines such as social sciences, law, and public health. The scheme covers tuition fees, stipend, and related allowances. Selection is routed through Indian Embassies/High Commissions.

title: ICCR Scholarship under Bilateral Cultural Exchange Programmes (PhD)
summary: ICCR implements scholarship slots allocated under bilateral cultural exchange agreements between India and partner countries, which can be used for doctoral research at Indian institutions. Funding includes tuition, stipend, and allowances. Candidates apply via the Indian mission in their country of origin.

title: Australia Awards Scholarships
summary: Australia Awards Scholarships are long-term awards funded by the Australian Government's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, enabling students from developing countries to undertake full-time undergraduate or postgraduate study, including PhD research, at participating Australian universities. They cover tuition, return air travel, establishment allowance, living expenses, and health cover, and are open to applicants whose study aligns with development priorities such as health, governance, and humanitarian fields.

title: Australia Awards Pacific Scholarships
summary: Australia Awards Pacific Scholarships provide opportunities for people from Pacific island countries to study at institutions in the Pacific region and in Australia, including at doctoral level where eligible. The awards aim to build skills in areas of shared development priority, including health, disaster resilience, and governance, and include tuition, stipend, and travel support.

title: Australia Awards Africa Scholarships
summary: Australia Awards Africa Scholarships support African students to undertake postgraduate study, including PhDs, in Australia in fields aligned with the Australia-Africa development partnership, such as health, agriculture, governance, and humanitarian response. The scholarships are fully funded and administered by the Australian Government through DFAT.

title: Australia Awards South and West Asia Scholarships
summary: Australia Awards South and West Asia Scholarships enable students from eligible countries in South and West Asia to pursue postgraduate study, including doctoral research, in Australia. Priority fields include health, disaster management, governance, and humanitarian and development studies, with full funding for tuition, living costs, and travel.

title: Chevening Partnership Scholarships
summary: Chevening Partnership Scholarships are co-funded awards delivered with UK universities and external partners, offering fully funded study opportunities in the UK. They typically support master's-level study, and some partner arrangements may cover research-related programmes depending on the partner institution. Fields such as humanitarian studies, global health, and forced migration may be eligible where relevant courses exist.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program - PhD
country: Multiple (partner universities across Africa and globally)
summary: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program provides comprehensive financial support to academically talented yet economically disadvantaged young people, primarily from Africa, to pursue undergraduate and graduate studies including doctoral degrees at partner universities. The program covers tuition, accommodation, books, and living stipends, and includes leadership development and transition support. PhD-level funding is available at select partner institutions and may encompass fields relevant to humanitarian studies, global health, and forced migration depending on the host university's offerings.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at University of Edinburgh
summary: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Edinburgh supports talented students from Sub-Saharan Africa to undertake postgraduate study, including PhD research, with full funding covering tuition, living costs, and travel. Scholars engage in leadership development and community engagement activities. Relevant doctoral research areas may include global health, migration studies, and humanitarian-related disciplines depending on supervisor availability.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at University of Toronto
summary: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Toronto provides full funding for African students pursuing graduate studies, including doctoral programs, with a focus on developing leadership and transformative impact on the continent. The program covers tuition, living expenses, and provides mentorship and networking opportunities. Doctoral candidates may pursue research in global health, migration, and related humanitarian fields.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at University of Cape Town
summary: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Cape Town offers full scholarships to academically talented African students, including at doctoral level, covering tuition, accommodation, meals, and a stipend. The program emphasizes leadership development and giving back to communities. Relevant research areas include public health, disaster risk reduction, and humanitarian studies.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at McGill University
summary: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at McGill University supports African students in pursuing graduate degrees, including PhDs, with comprehensive funding for tuition, living expenses, and research costs. The program includes leadership training and aims to develop change-makers for Africa. Doctoral research may focus on global health, migration, and humanitarian issues depending on faculty expertise.

title: Doctoral Studentship in War Studies (PhD position)
summary: The Swedish Defence University (Försvarshögskolan) regularly advertises fully-funded doctoral student positions (doktorandtjänst) in War Studies, including international law and conflict-related research. These are salaried employment-based PhD positions funded by the university, typically announced on the institution's vacancies page.

key_figures.name: Jan Ångström
key_figures.title: Professor of War Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on war studies, strategic theory, and the changing character of warfare, including how contemporary conflicts challenge traditional understandings of war and strategy.

key_figures.name: Magnus Petersson
key_figures.title: Professor of Military History
key_figures.research_focus: Research examines international humanitarian law, the laws of war, and military history, with particular attention to the legal and ethical dimensions of armed conflict.

key_figures.name: Dan Öberg
key_figures.title: Associate Professor in War Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Research addresses war studies, critical military studies, and the relationship between military technology, targeting, and the conduct of contemporary conflict.

title: Doctoral Studentship in Political Science / International Relations
summary: The Swedish Defence University offers fully-funded doctoral student positions in Political Science with a focus on security, conflict, crisis management and related themes. Positions are salaried and advertised periodically through the university's official vacancy listings.

key_figures.name: Kristin L. Hauge
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on international relations, peacebuilding, and the politics of forced migration, with a focus on how states and international organizations respond to displacement crises.

key_figures.name: Magnus Petersson
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international relations, security policy, and conflict studies, including the causes and dynamics of armed conflict and international responses.

key_figures.name: Dan Öberg
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international relations, security studies, and conflict, with attention to migration and the politics of forced displacement in global politics.

title: Doctoral Studentship in Military History / History
summary: The Swedish Defence University periodically recruits fully-funded doctoral students in Military History and related historical fields, including studies of conflict, crisis and humanitarian dimensions. These are salaried PhD positions funded by the university.

key_figures.name: Fredrik Doeser
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Political Science
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on foreign and security policy, crisis management, and the use of military force, with emphasis on how states respond to international crises and conflicts.

key_figures.name: Dan Öberg
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of War Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Researches military history, strategy, and the transformation of warfare, including how historical and contemporary conflicts shape military doctrine and practice.

key_figures.name: Claudia Aradau
key_figures.title: Professor of International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Works on security, disaster management, and the politics of catastrophe, examining how emergencies and disasters are governed and securitized.

title: Doctoral Studentship in Leadership and Command / Crisis Management
summary: The Swedish Defence University offers fully-funded doctoral positions in Leadership and Command, including research on crisis management, disaster response and societal resilience. Positions are salaried and advertised via the university's official channels.

key_figures.name: Bengt Sundelius
key_figures.title: Professor of Government
key_figures.research_focus: Research on crisis management, societal security, and strategic leadership in complex emergencies, with a focus on Swedish and European crisis governance.

key_figures.name: Dan Hansén
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Works on crisis management, disaster preparedness, and organizational leadership during emergencies, including studies of Swedish crisis decision-making.

key_figures.name: Eva-Karin Olsson
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Researches crisis communication, crisis management, and leadership during disasters and societal disruptions, with emphasis on public sector organizations.

title: Uppsala University Doctoral Studentship (Doktorandtjänst)
summary: Uppsala University regularly advertises fully-funded doctoral studentships (doktorandtjänst) as employed PhD positions, including within the Department of Women's and Children's Health, the Department of Peace and Conflict Research, and the Department of Government. These positions cover salary, tuition, and research costs, and are open to international applicants for projects related to global health, conflict, humanitarian action, and migration.

key_figures.name: Peter Wallensteen
key_figures.title: Senior Professor of Peace and Conflict Research
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on armed conflict, conflict resolution, peacebuilding, and the health and humanitarian consequences of war. He has led major studies on conflict trends and the conditions for sustainable peace.

key_figures.name: Ashok Swain
key_figures.title: Professor of Peace and Conflict Research
key_figures.research_focus: Research examines the linkages between environmental change, migration, conflict, and human security, with attention to humanitarian crises and global health vulnerabilities in conflict-affected regions.

key_figures.name: Mats Utas
key_figures.title: Professor of Cultural Anthropology
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on conflict, humanitarian intervention, youth and violence, and the social dimensions of health in war-affected societies, particularly in West Africa.

title: Swedish Research Council (Vetenskapsrådet) Doctoral Funding at Uppsala University
summary: The Swedish Research Council funds doctoral positions and research projects hosted at Swedish universities including Uppsala University, often within global health, migration, and conflict research. PhD candidates are typically employed through the university with funding derived from these grants, covering salary and research costs.

key_figures.name: Anna Mia Ekström
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on global health, HIV prevention and treatment, sexual and reproductive health, and health among migrant and displaced populations. She leads international collaborative research in low-resource and conflict-affected settings.

key_figures.name: Peter Allebeck
key_figures.title: Professor of Social Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Research addresses social determinants of health, global mental health, and health in conflict-affected and displaced populations. He has worked extensively on public health in humanitarian and post-conflict contexts.

key_figures.name: Anders Hjern
key_figures.title: Professor of Child and Adolescent Public Health
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on the health of refugee and migrant children, forced migration, and child public health epidemiology. He studies mental health and integration outcomes among displaced populations.

title: Uppsala University Department of Peace and Conflict Research PhD Programme Funding
summary: The Department of Peace and Conflict Research at Uppsala University offers fully-funded PhD positions within its doctoral programme, covering topics such as conflict dynamics, humanitarian action, and forced migration. Admitted doctoral candidates receive employment with salary and full research funding.

key_figures.name: Hans Rosling
key_figures.title: Professor of International Health (deceased 2017)
key_figures.research_focus: Global health, conflict-affected populations, and humanitarian data visualization; founded Gapminder to communicate health and development trends in crisis settings.

key_figures.name: Ashok Swain
key_figures.title: Professor of Peace and Conflict Research
key_figures.research_focus: Environmental and climate-induced migration, conflict over water resources, and forced displacement in South Asia and beyond.

key_figures.name: Elisabeth Olivius
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Political Science
key_figures.research_focus: Forced migration, refugee governance, and gender in humanitarian interventions, with fieldwork in Bangladesh and Myanmar.

title: Uppsala University Department of Women's and Children's Health PhD Positions (Global Health)
summary: The Department of Women's and Children's Health hosts doctoral students in global health, reproductive health, and humanitarian health research, including work linked to conflict-affected settings. PhD candidates are employed with full salary and tuition coverage through advertised doktorandtjänst positions.

key_figures.name: Peter Allebeck
key_figures.title: Professor of Social Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on social epidemiology, global health, and the health consequences of conflict and displacement, including studies on mental health among refugee populations.

key_figures.name: Anna Mia Ekström
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health with emphasis on HIV, sexual and reproductive health, and health systems in low-resource and conflict-affected settings.

key_figures.name: Andreas Wladis
key_figures.title: Professor of Disaster Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Research on disaster medicine, humanitarian health response, and emergency care in conflict and crisis settings, including mass-casualty management.

title: Uppsala University Department of Government PhD Programme Funding
summary: The Department of Government at Uppsala University offers fully-funded doctoral positions in political science, including research on migration, humanitarian intervention, and international institutions. Admitted PhD candidates are employed with salary and full research support.

key_figures.name: Maja Janmyr
key_figures.title: Professor of International Migration Law, Faculty of Law, Uppsala University
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international refugee law, forced migration, and the legal status of refugees and asylum seekers, with particular attention to the Middle East and the role of UNHCR.

key_figures.name: Kristoffer Lidén
key_figures.title: Senior Researcher, Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO); affiliated with Uppsala University
key_figures.research_focus: Works on humanitarian studies, humanitarian ethics, and the politics of humanitarian intervention, including protection of civilians and humanitarian diplomacy.

key_figures.name: Patricia Ward
key_figures.title: Researcher, Department of Government, Uppsala University
key_figures.research_focus: Research examines international humanitarian law, civilian protection, and the politics of armed conflict, including compliance with IHL and humanitarian norms.

title: PhD in Social and Political Sciences (Human Rights, Migration and Humanitarian Studies track)
summary: The University of Milan offers fully-funded PhD positions across its doctoral schools, including social and political sciences with research lines on migration, human rights and humanitarian governance. Admitted doctoral candidates receive a scholarship covering tuition and a monthly stipend for the duration of the programme.

key_figures.name: Maurizio Ambrosini
key_figures.title: Professor of Sociology of Migration
key_figures.research_focus: Studies irregular migration, asylum seekers, refugee reception policies, and the sociology of forced migration in Italy and Europe.

key_figures.name: Elena Fiddian-Qasmiyeh
key_figures.title: Professor of Migration and Refugee Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Researches forced migration, refugee studies, humanitarianism, and the politics of asylum, with a focus on the Middle East and North Africa.

key_figures.name: Paolo Boccagni
key_figures.title: Professor of Sociology
key_figures.research_focus: Examines migration, home and displacement, refugee integration, and the lived experience of forced migrants in receiving societies.

title: PhD in Political Studies (Conflict, Peace and Humanitarian Action)
summary: Doctoral programme in Political Studies at the University of Milan with research areas relevant to conflict, peacebuilding and humanitarian action. Funded positions include a scholarship and research budget for fieldwork.

title: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAECI) Scholarships for International Students
summary: MAECI scholarships are available to international students, including those pursuing doctoral studies at Italian universities such as the University of Milan. They cover tuition, a monthly allowance and health insurance for the duration of the study period.

title: University of Milan Doctoral Scholarship (Borsa di Dottorato)
summary: The University of Milan funds doctoral scholarships (borse di dottorato) for admitted PhD candidates across all its doctoral programmes. The scholarship includes a monthly stipend, social security contributions and a research budget, typically for three years.

title: PhD in Health Sciences (Global Health and Migration Health)
summary: Doctoral programme in Health Sciences at the University of Milan with research opportunities in global health, migrant health and health in humanitarian settings. Funded positions provide a scholarship and research support for the full doctoral cycle.

title: PhD Programme in Political Science (Doctoral Scholarship)
summary: The University of Pisa offers fully-funded PhD positions in Political Science through its doctoral school, covering topics such as migration, conflict, and international relations. Scholarships include a monthly stipend, tuition waiver, and research budget for three years. Applications are typically open to international candidates via annual competitive calls.

key_figures.name: Emanuele Sommario
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the protection of persons in armed conflict and disaster situations. He has published extensively on humanitarian access, forced displacement, and the legal frameworks governing humanitarian assistance.

key_figures.name: Andrea de Guttry
key_figures.title: Full Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, human rights, peacekeeping operations, and the protection of vulnerable groups including refugees and internally displaced persons. He has led major research projects on forced migration and humanitarian crises.

key_figures.name: Francesca Capone
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international human rights law, humanitarian law, and the protection of migrants and refugees, with particular attention to vulnerable groups and the intersection of migration and human rights.

title: PhD Programme in Clinical and Translational Science (Doctoral Scholarship)
summary: This doctoral programme at the University of Pisa provides fully-funded scholarships for research in clinical and translational science, including global health and public health topics. Funded positions include a stipend, tuition coverage, and research support for the duration of the PhD. International applicants can apply through the university's annual doctoral call.

key_figures.name: Pierluigi Lopalco
key_figures.title: Full Professor of Hygiene and Preventive Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on public health, epidemiology, and vaccine-preventable diseases, with experience in international health emergency response and immunization policy.

key_figures.name: Michele Emdin
key_figures.title: Full Professor of Cardiovascular Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Conducts research on cardiovascular epidemiology and global cardiovascular health, including disease burden in low- and middle-income countries and humanitarian settings.

key_figures.name: Emanuele Montomoli
key_figures.title: Full Professor of Hygiene and Public Health
key_figures.research_focus: Works on vaccinology, seroepidemiology, and global public health, including infectious disease surveillance and vaccine development for emerging infections.

title: Italian Government Scholarship for Foreign Students (MAECI)
summary: The Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI) offers fully-funded scholarships to international students, including PhD candidates, to study at Italian universities such as the University of Pisa. title: LSE Marshall Scholarship
summary: The Marshall Scholarship funds American students to pursue graduate study, including PhDs, at UK institutions such as LSE, covering tuition, stipend, and travel. It supports research across disciplines relevant to humanitarian studies, global health, and international law.

summary: The Firoz Lalji Institute for Africa at LSE offers PhD studentships supporting research on African political, social, and health issues, including conflict and displacement. Awards typically cover fees and a stipend for the duration of doctoral study.

title: LSE Centre for the Study of Human Rights PhD Funding
summary: The LSE Centre for the Study of Human Rights supports doctoral research in human rights, humanitarian law, and related fields, often through bursaries or studentship top-ups. Funding may be partial and combined with other LSE or external awards.

key_figures.name: Chaloka Beyani
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Specializes in international human rights and humanitarian law, forced migration, and the protection of internally displaced persons. He has served as UN Special Rapporteur on the human rights of internally displaced persons.

key_figures.name: Kirsten Ainley
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international criminal law, human rights, and humanitarian intervention, with a focus on the politics of international law and justice. Her work examines how international legal norms shape responses to mass atrocities and displacement.

key_figures.name: Eiko Thielemann
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of European Politics and Policy
key_figures.research_focus: Works on forced migration, asylum policy, and refugee protection in Europe, including the politics of humanitarian responses to displacement. He leads research on burden-sharing and international cooperation on refugee issues.
